newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault/Aerospatiale seen bidding for Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: Dassault/Aerospatiale seen bidding for Thomson-CSF.

text.p: French aerospace group Aerospatiale and fighter plane maker Dassault Aviation, which agreed main outlines of a merger last week, could bid for defence electronics group Thomson-CSF," Le Monde said Saturday.

"The government will have a favourable disposition towards a joint candidature of Aerospatiale and Dassault to take over defence electronics group Thomson-CSF," the afternoon newspaper said on the frontpage of its edition, dated Sunday December 22 and Monday December 23.
It said that according to the Ministry of Defence "this project, on which the two aerospace companies in the process of merging have been working since July, makes industrial sense."
The paper, which is among the best informed in France, said that Alcatel Alsthom had asked its advising banks to study the possibility of teaming up with the two aerospace groups.
Le Monde quoted Aerospatiale sources as saying that a link with Alcatel would make industrial sense while teaming up with Lagardere Groupe had not.
The government earlier this month suspended the privatisation of Thomson SA, which has a 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF and 100 percent of consumer electronics group Thomson Multimedia (TMM).

In October, the government said it prefered to sell Thomson SA to Lagardere and not to Alcatel. Lagardere had planned to merge Thomson-CSF with its own Matra Defense Espace business and would have sold TMM to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea. But the independent Privatisation Commission objected to the sale terms.

Le Monde said that the government would be willing to accept the new grouping because it wants to speed up the restructuring of France's defence industry in the light of the merger agreement between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas in the U.S.
